Subject: Hosted API: Renewal + Throughput Accelerator (commit increase & tier remap)

Hi Samira —

Nice speaking with you yesterday. Per our call I put together a compact proposal that aligns Nimbus Labs' renewal with the usage runway you outlined. High-level summary: 

- Current hosted commit: 2,000,000 tokens/month (Standard tier).
- Proposed commit: 5,000,000 tokens/month (Premium tier mapped to the new rate bands).
- Billing term: 12 months, early renewal effective 2027-06-01.
- Unit economics: blended rate reduces to $0.0018 per 1k tokens for committed volume; overage pricing and burst lanes outlined in the attached.
- Ramp plan: 50% of the uplift activates month 1; full commit in month 3. We can stage the ramp if you prefer.

Attached: nimbus_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal + SOW summary), usage_apr_may.csv (recent token usage).

Key asks from your side: confirmation of the target commit and whether you want the standard Premium SLA or the Dedicated-like latency guard (we can include a higher SLA for an additional fixed fee).

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm commit and ramp cadence.
2) I issue a DocuSign with the amendment and the adjusted invoice.
3) Procurement returns PO or signs the DocuSign; we provision the capacity per the ramp timeline.

If helpful I can propose an introductory promotional credit on the first monthly invoice while you ramp — would you like me to include that in the DocuSign?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through line items.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

If these are straightforward I can get back with PO timing.

Hi Samira — answering inline below and adding a couple clarifications: 

> 1) Burst capacity: during Black Friday-like spikes we need short-term burst above committed tokens for up to 48 hours. Can you confirm how burst lanes work (throttle behavior and rate applied)?

We offer a two-tier burst model for hosted:
- Short burst (temporary): automatic soft-burst for up to 72 hours that uses spare capacity at the Premium rate band; bursts are throttled by token/s per minute to preserve tail latencies.
- Emergency burst (manual): a manual capacity uplift we can enable for a defined window with a separate charge (we've used this for other customers during promotional spikes).

For Nimbus specifically, the proposal includes a 20% burst pocket (on top of committed tokens) charged at the overage rate of $0.0026 per 1k tokens; if you prefer a guaranteed emergency uplift we can add a one-time activation fee instead of overage pricing.

> 2) Price per 1k tokens: your note says $0.0018 blended — is that post-discount committed rate only, and what is the overage rate?

Correct — $0.0018 is the blended committed rate after the 12-month commit discount. Overage (consumption beyond the committed monthly allocation) is $0.0026 per 1k tokens by default; we can tier down overage pricing with a higher committed ladder if you expect sustained bursts.

> 3) Data retention and audit: our security team asked whether logs and request bodies are retained beyond 30 days for hosted customers (we cannot extend beyond 30 without an executed addendum).

We retain request bodies and logs for 30 days by default for hosted customers. If you need a different retention period we can add an RPO addendum in the contract; for Nimbus we can commit to 30 days in the SOW and include a clause for extended retention only after a signed addendum.

> Also procurement asked if we can get a single consolidated invoice per month (yes/no).

Yes — we can send one consolidated invoice per month. We'll include commit usage, overages, and any activation fees on the single invoice.

I updated the proposal to include the 20% burst pocket and clarified the overage rates — attached is a one-page summary and a DocuSign link to the amendment. If procurement is ready, please ask them to attach the PO to the DocuSign signing flow or reply with the PO number and I'll ensure we map it to the invoice.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/1234-REDWOOD-NIMBUS-proposal
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/records/92471-deal/DL-2027-0987

Would you like me to schedule a 15-min call with our support lead to talk SLA latencies and burst throttles?

Best,
